question_stem:
Two capacitors A and B are connected into the circuit shown in Fig. 5.1.

{{figure:9702_s23_42_q05_figure_5_1}}

Capacitor A has capacitance $C$ and capacitor B has capacitance $3C$.
The electromotive force (e.m.f.) of the cell is $V$.
The two-way switch S is initially at position X, and capacitor B is initially uncharged.

parts.label: (a)(i)
parts.part_stem: State, in terms of $V$ and $C$, expressions for:
parts.text: the initial charge $Q_{A}$ on the plates of capacitor A

parts.label: (a)(ii)
parts.text: the initial energy $E_{A}$ stored in capacitor A.

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.part_stem: The two-way switch S is now moved to position Y.
parts.text: State and explain what happens to the charge that was initially on the plates of capacitor A.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.text:
Show that the final potential difference (p.d.) $V_{B}$ across capacitor B is given by
$$V_{B} = \frac{V}{4}.$$
Explain your reasoning.

parts.label: (b)(iii)
parts.text: Determine an expression, in terms of $V$ and $C$, for the decrease $\Delta E$ in the total energy that is stored in the capacitors as a result of the change of the position of the switch.
